title: MCP apply defaults auto_accept=true — silently overwrites divergent configs (data loss)
description: selfie_apply_dotfiles (MCP) defaults auto_accept=true, which auto-accepts DeployDecision::Conflict and overwrites the target (service.rs:661). A Conflict happens when a target exists, has no local deploy-state (NotTracked), and its content DIFFERS from the repo source — exactly the fresh-second-machine case (e.g. deploying home's configs onto the work machine, which has its own unpushed edits). Result: the other machine's config is silently clobbered with NO prompt. This violates the 'no silent failures / no data loss' principle and is worst on the AI-native path (the primary use case). Fix: when there is no interactive resolver (MCP/headless), the SAFE default must be to SKIP conflicts and report them (auto_accept=false), requiring explicit opt-in to overwrite. Consider also surfacing the diff in the conflict event so an AI/user can decide. Surfaced 2026-07-23 reasoning through cross-machine deploy safety.
close_reason: MCP apply now defaults auto_accept=false; conflicts skipped+reported with diff. Fixed in 3238cd6, test apply_param_defaults_auto_accept_to_false

title: Validate environment-specific dotfiles + surface overrides in spec validation
description: ADR-0001 requires: 'Validation must surface environment overrides and missing sources rather than applying them silently.' validate_dotfiles currently only checks top-level (shared) dotfiles. Extend it to also structurally validate each environments.<name>.dotfiles entry (empty/traversal/relative-source/absolute-target checks — extract a per-entry helper), and emit a warning when an environment entry overrides a shared entry's target so the override is not silent. TDD. Follow-up to per-environment dotfiles core (34558ef).
close_reason: Env-specific dotfiles now structurally validated + overrides surfaced as warnings. Implemented in feat(validate) with 3 TDD tests.

title: Secret provider integration point for dotfiles (shell out to 1Password/teller, don't reinvent)
description: ADR-0001 Problem B. selfie must NOT build its own secret store/encryption/templating. Instead provide an integration point that resolves a dotfile's content by running a user-configured provider command at apply time (e.g. 'op read op://vault/item/field', teller). Fits selfie's command-runner identity. DotfileEntry content source becomes: repo file (source) OR provider command (secret/from ref). At apply, run the provider, write result to target; never commit or persist the secret value; drift/state must NOT store the secret's checksum/value (needs distinct semantics - part of this design). Use case: private RubyGems server creds on work machine. User standardizes on 1Password (personal+work) and teller (work GCP/dotenv). Detailed design deferred; depends on selfie-7sv (per-env dotfiles) landing the content-source abstraction. Relates to selfie-t2d (multiple package dirs / private overlay).

title: Dotfiles are single-source, not per-environment — no machine-specific config variants (YADM alt-file parity)
description: The 'dotfiles' field is top-level (one 'source' per mapping, deployed to all environments). If home and work legitimately need DIFFERENT versions of a config (e.g. ghostty font size, work-specific proxy settings), selfie cannot represent both — there is a single canonical source. YADM handles this via alt-files (##os.Linux, ##hostname) and templates. For selfie's home+work cross-machine goal this is a structural gap: today the user must unify configs across machines or they'll conflict on deploy. Options to design: per-environment dotfile overrides/variants, templating, or an explicit 'shared vs machine-specific' split. Relates to selfie-522 (environment inheritance). Surfaced 2026-07-23.
design: Per-environment dotfiles (ADR-0001, Problem A). Add optional 'dotfiles: Vec<DotfileEntry>' to EnvironmentConfig. Effective set for current env = top-level shared dotfiles, with any entry whose resolved target matches an env-specific entry REPLACED by it, unioned with env-specific entries introducing new targets. Env-specific overrides shared keyed on target; otherwise added (presence). No exclusion (YAGNI). Source resolution unchanged (relative to package YAML dir). git identity is out of scope (use git-native includeIf). DotfileEntry to gain a content-source abstraction so it composes with secret providers (selfie-B). No backward compat (pre-release).
notes: Core per-environment dotfiles (model + effective-set + apply/drift wiring + tests + docs) landed in 34558ef. Remaining per ADR-0001 tracked as blockers: selfie-chi (validation + override surfacing), selfie-2m1 (list/track/remove consistency).
close_reason: Per-environment dotfiles delivered in 34558ef (EnvironmentConfig.dotfiles + effective-set override/presence + apply/drift wiring + tests + docs; ADR-0001). Single-source limitation resolved. Refinements tracked independently: selfie-chi (env-dotfile validation + override surfacing), selfie-2m1 (list/track/remove consistency).

title: track_dotfile records target as expanded absolute path, breaking cross-machine portability
description: selfie_package_track_dotfile (MCP) and 'selfie track' (CLI) record the dotfile 'target' as a fully-expanded absolute path containing the literal home dir, e.g. 'target: /Users/sloveless/.config/ghostty/config', instead of a portable '~/.config/ghostty/config'. This breaks the core cross-machine value prop: on a machine with a different username (macos-work uses 'steve.loveless') or OS (Linux /home/...), the target resolves to the wrong/nonexistent path. Hand-written specs correctly use '~'. Fix: when tracking, store the target relative to $HOME using '~' (collapse the home prefix) rather than the expanded absolute path. Surfaced 2026-07-23 migrating ghostty/fastfetch/marksman/yamllint/zed via MCP; topgrade had the same issue from earlier tracking.

title: Config loader warns on unknown/ignored keys instead of silently dropping them

This hid a broken dotfiles setup for the user. Per user principle: selfie must NOT fail silently — if it can proceed with a funky-but-usable config, it should, but it must emit a warning about ignored/unknown keys (via the event system, not stdout, per the library boundary rules). Applies to both CLI and MCP frontends.

title: Rename max_parallel_installations to max_concurrency and apply everywhere
description:
Two problems:

1. **Misleading name**: `max_parallel_installations` is not used for installations at all — only for concurrent checks in `list` and dep status checks in `status`.

2. **Inconsistent usage**: Several operations that do concurrent work don't honor it — notably `install` (which the name implies it should) and any future bulk operations.

Fix both: rename to `max_concurrency` and apply the semaphore/chunking pattern to all concurrent operations including install. No backward compatibility needed (no releases yet). Affects: config structs, YAML deserialization, CLI config display, install handler, docs, CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: Renamed max_parallel_installations to max_concurrency, applied concurrency to audit_all and install_recommends, dropped num_cpus dep. PR #41.

title: Show dependency satisfaction status in package info
description:
When displaying package info (info, list, check commands), indicate whether the package's declared dependencies are actually installed. Currently dependencies are listed in the info command but there's no indication of whether they're satisfied.

This would run the check command for each dependency and show a per-dep status (installed/not installed/unknown). Helps users catch broken dependency chains before attempting an install.

Implementation considerations:
- This is essentially running check on each dep, so it should reuse the existing check logic via PackageService.
- For the list command, this could be expensive if every package's deps are checked — consider making it opt-in (e.g., --check-deps flag) or only showing it in info/verbose modes.
- Emit dependency status via PackageEvent so CLI and MCP can render it.
- Handle missing deps gracefully (dep package file doesn't exist vs dep not installed).
close_reason: Implemented dependency satisfaction status in the status command. Added DependencyStatus struct, concurrent dep checking via execute_check_command_quiet, CLI rendering with colored status, and MCP JSON serialization. 5 new tests covering all edge cases.

title: Show git-dirty indicator on package info commands
description:
Commands that display package information (info, list, check, validate, audit) should also indicate whether the local package YAML file has uncommitted git changes. This helps users notice when their package specs have been modified locally but not yet committed, which matters for keeping configs in sync across machines.

Scope: Add a git-status indicator (e.g., 'modified', 'untracked', 'staged') to package output in commands that report package details. The indicator should appear alongside existing package metadata.

Implementation considerations:
- The selfie library has no git functionality today — this is net-new.
- Following hexagonal architecture, git operations should go behind a trait/port (e.g., GitStatusProvider) so the CLI can use a real implementation and tests can mock it.
- The library should emit git status info via PackageEvent so each frontend (CLI, MCP) can render it appropriately.
- Need to handle: file is untracked, file has staged changes, file has unstaged changes. Also handle gracefully when the package directory is not a git repo.
- Skip unpushed detection — committed is sufficient. This avoids complexity around missing upstream tracking branches.
- Performance: for the list command, checking git status for many files should be efficient (e.g., one 'git status --porcelain' call for the whole directory, not one per file).
close_reason: Implemented and merged in PR #28

description: Rename MCP tools: selfie_get_package→selfie_spec_info, selfie_validate_package→selfie_spec_validate, selfie_create_package→selfie_spec_create, selfie_update_package→selfie_spec_update, selfie_remove_package→selfie_spec_remove. Add selfie_package_status. Update server struct to use both traits.
close_reason: Code already implements this — CLI split, MCP tool renames, and test updates are all in place on main

title: Split CLI command structure into spec + package groups
description: Add SpecSubcommands enum and SpecCommands struct to cli.rs. Move create/edit/remove/validate to selfie spec. Replace info with status under selfie package. Create commands/spec/ module directory. Add dispatch_spec_command() to commands.rs.
close_reason: Closed

title: Split 'selfie package' into 'selfie spec' + 'selfie package'
description: The package command namespace is overloaded — it mixes file/definition operations (create, edit, remove, validate, update) with runtime operations (install, check, audit, list). Split into 'selfie spec' for file ops and 'selfie package' for runtime ops. Clean break, no backward compat. See plan file: .claude/plans/purrfect-mixing-sonnet.md
close_reason: Code already implements this — CLI split, MCP tool renames, and test updates are all in place on main

title: Wire start_operation spinner into install and check commands
description: P2: list has spinner support, but install and check — the commands that actually run shell commands and might take seconds to minutes — just print a dim static line and go silent until completion. start_operation() exists and is fully implemented but marked #[allow(dead_code)]. Wire it into install and check event handlers for proper progress feedback during long-running operations.
close_reason: Spinners wired into check and install commands

title: Create unified result card / section header pattern
description: P2: Each command invented its own 'show structured data' format. check uses 📋 header + 3-space format_key_fn, validate success uses same but different, validate issues uses comfy_table, info uses bare comfy_table, config validate uses print_field (2-space, italic dim). Create DisplayManager::print_section_header() and a standardized card renderer to unify the visual language across check, validate, info, and config validate.
close_reason: ResultCard builder added, check/validate/audit refactored

title: CLI Design Consistency Epic
description: Comprehensive CLI output and UX consistency improvements identified during design review. The CLI has good architectural foundations (DisplayManager, EventProcessor, status_style) but inconsistent application across commands. This epic covers routing all output through DisplayManager, standardizing symbols, creating unified result card patterns, wiring spinners into more commands, and fixing various small inconsistencies.
close_reason: All child issues complete — epic done

title: YAML merge keys (<<: *anchor) not supported by serde_yaml 0.9
description: serde_yaml 0.9 dropped support for YAML merge keys (<<: *anchor) that existed in 0.8. This breaks package files that use anchors to DRY environment configs (e.g. homebrew.yml with _mac: &mac and <<: *mac). The error is now visible thanks to the ParseError display fix, but the underlying issue remains. Options: (1) switch to serde_yml crate (maintained fork with merge key support), (2) pre-process YAML to resolve merge keys before deserialization, (3) document the limitation and suggest users avoid merge keys.
close_reason: Closing as not-a-bug: package files use YAML anchors (&anchor/*anchor) which work fine with serde_yaml 0.9. No files use merge keys (<<: *anchor) which was the hypothesized issue. Unable to reproduce the original problem.

title: Remove async-trait — use native async traits + upgrade mockall to 0.14.0
description:
Remove async-trait crate; use Rust's native async fn in traits (stable since 1.75). Upgrade mockall from 0.13.1 to 0.14.0 which supports native async trait mocking.

Files using #[async_trait]: commands/runner.rs, commands/shell.rs, package/service.rs (×2), config/loader.rs. Note: ConfigLoader uses #[async_trait] but has no async methods — can just remove it.

Mocked async traits: CommandRunner (4 async methods), PackageService (7 async methods). Both use #[automock] + #[async_trait] together.

Benefit: Removes heap allocation per async trait call, removes a dependency, uses idiomatic modern Rust.

Risk: mockall 0.14.0 is a major version bump — may have breaking API changes beyond async trait support. Run full test suite after upgrade.
close_reason: Removed async-trait, upgraded mockall to 0.14, native RPITIT async traits, fixed mock visibility and hardcoded shell path

title: OperationFailure duplicates PackageError types field-for-field
description: OperationFailure has variants like PackageFailure::NotFound that mirror PackageError::PackageNotFound field-for-field, creating a parallel error hierarchy. When an error occurs, the same information exists in both PackageError and OperationFailure. OperationFailure should reference or wrap PackageError rather than duplicating its structure. Related to selfie-mqq (double event emission).
close_reason: Merged EnvironmentFailure and PackageFailure enums into OperationFailure::Package(PackageError) wrapper. Deleted ~130 lines of duplicate type definitions and field-copying conversion code.

title: Implement PackageService::create or remove from trait
description: PackageService::create is declared in the trait but the implementation is a stub that returns a placeholder success. The CLI's create.rs bypasses the service entirely and uses PackageRepository directly — the most significant hexagonal architecture boundary violation. Either implement create properly in the service (with event streaming, validation, etc.) or remove it from the trait until ready.
close_reason: PackageService::create is now fully implemented with service handler, event variants, and CLI integration

title: Add tests for ConfigLoader and YamlLoader
description: config/loader.rs (ConfigLoader trait, ConfigLoadError) and config/yaml.rs (YamlLoader) have zero tests. This is the component responsible for finding and reading the config file on disk — a critical path with several error variants (NotFound, MultipleFound, ConfigError) that are never exercised in isolation. config/validate.rs also lacks unit tests (only tested through CLI integration tests).
close_reason: Added 10 tests covering all validation paths in config/validate.rs

title: Fix double event emission for errors
description: When an error occurs, the library emits it twice: once as PackageEvent::Error and again inside PackageEvent::Completed { result: Failure } with a re-serialized copy in OperationFailure. This forces the CLI to implement PackageNotFoundTracker as a suppression workaround in common.rs. The Completed event should reference the error, not duplicate it. Additionally, OperationFailure duplicates error types field-for-field (e.g., PackageFailure::NotFound mirrors PackageError::PackageNotFound).
close_reason: Fixed in db33934: eliminated double event emission and removed PackageNotFoundTracker workaround

title: Unify PackageService return types across all methods
description: PackageService methods have inconsistent return types: check/install return EventStream directly, while info/validate/list return Result<EventStream, PackageError>. All methods should use the same pattern. Either all return EventStream (encoding early-exit errors as the first event in the stream) or all return Result<EventStream>. The inconsistency forces callers to handle two different patterns.
close_reason: Already fixed in commits 1cbab63, db33934, 9ca8c98, d9ce8a1. All six PackageService methods now uniformly return EventStream directly.

title: CLI commands should accept Box<dyn PackageService> for testability
description: CLI command handlers use the concrete type PackageServiceImpl<YamlPackageRepository<RealFileSystem>, ShellCommandRunner> via create_package_service() in common.rs. This prevents injecting MockPackageService for unit testing. Commands should accept Box<dyn PackageService> (dynamic dispatch) so mock services can be used in tests. MockPackageService and MockCommandRunner are defined but never used because of this.
close_reason: Refactored all 6 CLI command handlers to accept &dyn PackageService parameter instead of creating service internally. Service creation now happens at the dispatch_package_command level in commands.rs.

title: Fix event_processor tests using real filesystem
description: event_processor.rs tests (lines 328-418) create real ShellCommandRunner and RealFileSystem instances pointing at /tmp/nonexistent. These tests depend on filesystem state and could behave differently in CI. Replace with mock-based tests for deterministic behavior.
close_reason: Already fixed: tests now use stream::iter(vec![...]) to construct EventStream directly, with no real filesystem or command runner dependencies.

title: Audit console/dialoguer in library crate dependencies
description: The console and dialoguer crates are listed as dependencies of the selfie library crate (Cargo.toml). These are terminal UI crates that don't appear to be used in the library's production code. Verify usage and move to [dev-dependencies] or remove entirely -- these belong only in the CLI crate.
close_reason: Removed unused console dependency from selfie library Cargo.toml

title: Encapsulate GetPackage fields
description: GetPackage has pub fields (package, file_path, is_new) rather than accessor methods. The CLI's create.rs constructs GetPackage directly, bypassing any encapsulation. Make fields pub(crate) and provide public constructors/accessors, similar to how Package is already designed. This is API hygiene for v1.
close_reason: Encapsulated GetPackage fields and implemented PackageService::create

title: dotfiles list/track/remove should reflect per-environment dotfiles
description: The per-environment dotfiles core (34558ef) wired apply + drift to the effective set, but 'dotfiles list' (CLI list.rs, MCP server.rs) and the track/remove readers still use package.dotfiles() (shared only), so environment-specific dotfiles do not appear in listings and are not considered by remove's cleanup/track's display. Decide list semantics (effective set for current env, or list all with an environment label) and update accordingly. Follow-up to per-environment dotfiles core.
close_reason: list (CLI+MCP), track, and remove now use Package::dotfiles_with_scope() to reflect environment-specific dotfiles; CLI Environment column + MCP environment field; TDD.

title: Richer dotfile conflict resolution (backup-then-overwrite, merge) beyond accept/skip
description: On an apply conflict (existing target differs from selfie's source and may be user-authored), selfie currently offers accept (overwrite) or skip, and shows a unified diff. Enhancement: offer safer/richer resolution options, e.g. back up the existing target (.bak) before overwriting, open a merge tool / 3-way merge, or apply per-hunk. The core safety guarantee (never overwrite divergent content without consent) already holds and is recorded in ADR-0001 (Overwrite safety); this is about better ergonomics when a conflict does occur. The diff is already produced; merging is the hard part. Raised 2026-07-23 during ADR-0001 review.

title: selfie requires a config file to exist even when all settings are passed via CLI flags
description: During fresh-machine recovery proof (2026-07-23): running 'selfie apply' with HOME pointed at a clean dir failed with 'No configuration file found in locations: <HOME>/.config/selfie' even though --package-directory, --environment, and --state-directory were all supplied on the CLI. selfie should be able to run fully from CLI flags (and/or env vars) with no config file present — important for fresh-machine bootstrap, scripted/bulk operations, CI, containers, and ephemeral AI-driven runs. Workaround today: create ~/.config/selfie/config.yml first. Consider: treat missing config file as empty-config when required values come from flags, or add a way to point at an explicit config path.

title: CLI: add non-interactive way to attach a dotfile to an existing package (parity with MCP selfie_dotfiles_add)
description: 'selfie track <file>' is fully interactive (prompts existing-package vs standalone) with no flags to bypass it, so it can't be scripted or used in automation/bulk migration. The MCP server already has a non-interactive 'selfie_dotfiles_add' (add file to an existing package's dotfiles section). Add a CLI equivalent, e.g. 'selfie dotfiles add <file> --package <name>' or non-interactive flags on 'track'. Surfaced 2026-07-23 while migrating bat off YADM. Lower priority since the AI/MCP path is the primary driver, but needed for scriptable bulk migration of ~170 dotfiles.

title: Audit selfie for other silent-failure paths; make them warn or error
description: Follow-up to the config-unknown-keys bug. Sweep the codebase for places where selfie swallows errors or degrades silently (e.g. best-effort steps that skip without notice, ignored parse results, dropped fields). Each should surface a warning/error via PackageEvent so the user is never surprised. Establishes 'no silent failures' as a selfie design value. Reference: strategic-direction memory + docs runbook 2026-07-23.

title: Implement environment name completer
description: Create a custom completer for the --environment/-e global flag that suggests known environment names. These can be extracted by scanning package files for their environment keys. This is lower priority than package name completion but still useful — users often forget exact environment labels.

title: Consider suppressing redundant success message on completion
description: After commands like `selfie package status`, the default Completed event handler prints a line like `✓ Package 'foo' status checked successfully (2/2 steps)`. This is redundant when the command already displayed its results (e.g., the status table). Consider suppressing or shortening this message for commands where the output itself implies success.
close_reason: Suppressed redundant success messages in status, info, audit, and check commands

title: Expand SelfieConfig validation
description: Current config validation only checks environment (non-empty) and package_directory (non-empty, absolute). Add validation for dotfiles_directory and state_directory (absolute path when set), and validate that command_timeout is reasonable (warn if >600s). Also consider validating that package_directory and dotfiles_directory exist on disk (as warnings, not errors).
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove custom validation code after garde adoption
description: Once garde handles validation via derive macros, remove: validate.rs hand-written validators, ValidationIssue/ValidationIssues types (replaced by garde's error types), the extra_fields serde(flatten) hack for unknown field detection (serde-saphyr + garde handles this natively). This is cleanup after the garde migration.
close_reason: Superseded — garde not being adopted, so there's no custom validation code to remove after adoption.

title: Improve CI workflow
description:
The CI workflow needs several improvements:
1. (DONE) Double-run fixed — push: now filtered to main only.
2. Add clippy job — it's in the pre-commit checklist but not in CI.
3. The format job auto-commits and pushes on failure, which triggers another CI run. Should just fail instead (let developers fix locally).
4. Consider adding cargo cache for faster builds.
5. Consider adding a Rust toolchain cache.
close_reason: Fixed in c31bf34. Added clippy, rust-cache, removed auto-push, cleaned up job names and deps.

title: Surface drift-check failures in sync status
description: collect_drift_summary() ignores OperationResult::Failure from the drift stream, causing sync status to report empty/zero drift values and overall success when drift checking actually failed. Should surface the failure as a warning event. Copilot PR #35 comment 2978720110.
close_reason: Fixed: collect_drift_summary now captures OperationResult::Failure and emits a warning event

title: Convert fast_forward to native gix ref update + checkout
description: fast_forward currently shells out to git merge --ff-only. Convert to native gix: verify ancestor relationship, update ref, then checkout working tree via gix-worktree-state. Requires adding worktree-state feature to gix dependency. User accepts larger binary for consistency.

title: Convert push/fetch to native gix transport
description: push and fetch currently shell out to git CLI for SSH/credential integration. Convert to gix's blocking-network-client transport. Requires adding the blocking-network-client feature to gix dependency. User accepts larger binary for consistency. May need to handle SSH agent integration via gix-transport.
notes: Assessment (2026-03-24, gix 0.81.0): Push is still incomplete in gix 0.81.0 — thin pack creation works but actual push protocol is not implemented. Fetch works with blocking-network-client feature but adds binary size and complexity for marginal benefit over reliable git CLI shell-out. Recommend revisiting when gix push matures (track gitoxide releases). The gix upgrade from 0.72→0.81 was done separately.

title: Convert remaining run_git calls to native gix
description: stage_files and commit are now pure gix. Remaining run_git calls for local ops that should be converted: discover_repo (branch via rev-parse, remote name), repo_status (ls-files --deleted), diff_commits (diff --name-status), ahead_behind_counts (rev-list). Network ops (push, fetch) and fast_forward (merge --ff-only) are fine as shell-outs.

title: Update docs for sync commands
description: Update README.md status section, docs/configuration.md with sync commands. Add docs/sync.md with usage examples for status/push/pull, flag reference, conventional commit format explanation, and MCP tool descriptions.
close_reason: Added docs/sync.md with complete sync guide. Updated README.md status section and navigation. dprint formatted.

title: Add requires_sudo flag per environment in package specs
description: Allow package specs to declare requires_sudo: true per environment, so selfie can warn or prompt before running commands that need elevated privileges. Nice UX touch for packages that need sudo on some environments but not others. Found in selfie2 old repo.

title: Support multiple package directories in config
description: Allow configuring multiple package_directory paths (e.g., a personal directory and a shared team directory). Packages from all directories would be discovered and available. Current config only supports a single package_directory. Found in selfie-v1, selfie2, and investigation-selfie old repos.

title: Auto-detect installation source from executable path
description: Enhance the audit system with a fallback heuristic that detects how a package was installed by examining its executable path. For example: /opt/homebrew/bin/ → brew, ~/.cargo/bin/ → cargo, /usr/local/bin/ → manual/unknown. This would provide audit info even when no explicit audit command is defined in the package spec. Found in narcissist and investigation-selfie old repos.

title: Add search command to find packages by keyword
description: Add a 'search' or 'spec search' command that searches package files by name, description, tags, or other metadata. Useful once the user has many packages defined. Found in selfie2 spec (was planned but not implemented).
close_reason: Implemented spec search command with case-insensitive substring matching on name and description

title: Add per-environment configs to package specs
description: Currently configs is a top-level field that applies across all environments. Add support for per-environment config entries so users can deploy different config files per environment (e.g. ~/.gitconfig-personal on personal machines, ~/.gitconfig-work on work machines). Design should follow whatever pattern the environment inheritance feature establishes, rather than inventing a separate filtering mechanism. Blocked by environment inheritance design.

title: Remove version field from package YAML schema
description: The version field in package definitions is vestigial — selfie never compares versions, there's no upgrade logic, and git tracks definition history better than a hand-bumped semver. Remove it entirely: drop from Package struct, remove from validation, stop emitting in spec create, update parser to ignore if present (don't break existing files). If we later need schema versioning (post-release), add a schema_version or selfie_min_version field at that point.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #32

title: Investigate flattening CLI command structure
description: Evaluate moving runtime package commands to top-level: 'selfie install X' instead of 'selfie package install X'. Now that groups are off the table (replaced by recommends), the 'package' namespace adds typing without value for the hot-path commands (install, check, audit). Questions to answer: (1) What happens to 'selfie list' ambiguity (specs vs packages)? (2) Should 'selfie package list' and 'selfie spec list' stay namespaced? (3) Keep 'selfie package X' as aliases during transition or break cleanly? (4) How does this affect MCP server tool naming? (5) Does 'selfie apply' already set the precedent for top-level verbs?

title: Investigate flattening CLI command structure (selfie install vs selfie package install)
description:
Now that 'selfie group' commands are off the table (replaced by recommends), the 'selfie package' namespace may be unnecessary overhead for the most common commands. Investigate promoting runtime verbs to top-level:

- selfie install ripgrep (instead of selfie package install ripgrep)
- selfie check ripgrep
- selfie audit ripgrep
- selfie apply ripgrep (already top-level)

Open questions to resolve:
- What happens to 'selfie list'? Ambiguous between spec list and package list. Maybe defaults to package list with status?
- Should 'selfie package install' remain as an alias for backward compat, or break it (pre-1.0)?
- Does the spec subcommand stay as-is? (Probably yes — definition management is less frequent)
- How does this affect the MCP server tool naming?
- Impact on shell completions and help text organization
- Does 'selfie status' make sense as top-level too?

This is an investigation ticket — answer the questions, then decide whether to proceed.
close_reason: Duplicate of selfie-gyb

title: Rename package config deployment to 'dotfile' terminology
description:
The word 'config' is overloaded in the codebase: SelfieConfig (selfie's settings), ConfigEntry/ConfigService (package file deployment), and the 'selfie config' CLI subcommand. Rename the package config deployment layer to use 'dotfile' instead.

Scope of changes:
- YAML schema: configs: → dotfiles:, configs_directory → dotfiles_directory in selfie config
- Types: ConfigEntry → DotfileEntry, ConfigService → DotfileService, ConfigServiceImpl → DotfileServiceImpl
- Module: config_service/ → dotfile_service/ (or dotfile/)
- Events: ConfigDeploying → DotfileDeploying, ConfigDeployed → DotfileDeployed, etc.
- CLI: apply command internals (the 'selfie apply' command name stays the same)
- MCP server: tool names and descriptions that reference 'config' in the deployment sense
- Docs: package-files.md, configuration.md, README examples
- Tests: all config_service_tests

This is a pure rename refactor with no behavior changes. Should be done as a focused PR separate from feature work.
close_reason: Duplicate of selfie-ybf

title: Track and display last check/install timestamps
description:
Persist timestamps for when each package was last checked or installed, and display this in info/list output. Helps users identify stale packages that haven't been verified in a while.

This is a larger feature because selfie currently has no persistent state beyond the package YAML files and config. It requires a new storage mechanism for run history.

Implementation considerations:
- Need a state/history store — likely a simple JSON or SQLite file in the selfie config directory (~/.config/selfie/state.db or similar).
- Following hexagonal architecture, the state store should be behind a trait/port (e.g., RunHistoryProvider).
- Record: package name, operation type (check/install/audit), timestamp, result (success/failure).
- Display in info command: 'Last checked: 3 days ago', 'Last installed: 2 weeks ago'.
- Display in list command: optional column or indicator for staleness.
- Consider a --stale flag for list to filter packages not checked within N days.
- The MCP server should also be able to query this data.

title: Detect package manager availability before install
description:
Before running install/check/audit commands, detect whether the package manager binary (e.g., brew, npm, apt) referenced in the command actually exists on the system. Surface this as an early warning in info and list output rather than waiting for a cryptic command-not-found error at install time.

The codebase already has an is_command_available function using the which crate. This feature would parse the first token of install/check/audit commands to identify the binary, then check availability.

Implementation considerations:
- Parse the first token of each command string to extract the binary name. Handle pipes (use the first command), shell wrappers, etc.
- For list command, could show a warning indicator next to packages whose commands reference unavailable binaries.
- For info command, show per-environment binary availability.
- Emit via PackageEvent for frontend-agnostic rendering.
- Performance: which lookups are fast, but cache results since many packages may use the same binary (e.g., dozens of brew packages).

title: Install progress step count is wrong when dependencies are already installed
description: When running 'selfie package install', the total step count is calculated assuming every dependency needs full installation (fetch + env check + check + install command + verify). But dependencies that are already installed skip the install/verify steps, so the final count ends up lower than the total (e.g., '21/29 steps' when the operation is complete). The ProgressTracker total should be adjusted as dependencies are skipped, or the calculation should account for already-installed deps.
close_reason: ProgressTracker::reduce_total_steps(4) called when package already installed, correcting inflated step count

title: config validate checks post-override config, not on-disk file
description: The 'config validate' command validates config.selfie_config() after CLI overrides have been applied. This can mask problems in the on-disk config file (e.g., an invalid package_directory that becomes valid only due to a CLI flag override). Consider loading the raw file config inside this handler and validating that instead of the already-overridden CliConfig.
close_reason: handle_validate re-loads raw config from disk via YamlLoader instead of validating post-override config

title: handle_install returns was_already_installed=false for root package
description: handle_install in service/install.rs always returns OperationSuccess::package_installed(..., was_already_installed = false, executable_path = None) for the root package, even if the root was already installed. This loses information and can cause the CLI to report the wrong final status for no-op installs. Should track the root package's actual install result and use that when returning the final OperationResult.
close_reason: handle_install now returns the actual root package result instead of hardcoded was_already_installed=false

title: Fix verbose mode parity for check command
description: P3: install.rs forwards Progress events to default handler when verbose (returns false), but check.rs always suppresses Progress events (returns true) even in verbose mode. Users who set --verbose expect more output. check should forward Progress events to the default handler when verbose, matching install behavior.
close_reason: Implemented in commit a8ac5ff on feat/cli-display-consistency branch

title: Standardize indentation levels across output
description: P3: Three different indentation levels carry overlapping meanings. print_progress uses 2 spaces, print_field uses 2 spaces, check/validate format_key_fn uses 3 spaces, OperationHandle::add_output_line uses 2 spaces + │. Same visual concept (nested content / key-value pairs) uses different alignment. Pick one indentation for nested content and standardize.
close_reason: INDENT constant standardizes key-value indentation

title: Fix symbol semantic mismatches
description: P3: Two places use symbols with wrong semantics. 1) remove.rs:43 — print_info('✓ Package is not a dependency...') embeds success ✓ inside blue info message; should use print_success. 2) check.rs:106 — '⚠️ Check failed' uses warning symbol for a failure; symbol system says ✗ = failure, ⚠ = warning.
close_reason: Fixed print_info→print_success in remove.rs:48

title: Route static output through MultiProgress when spinners active
description: Phase 2 of indicatif display layer: DisplayManager's static output methods (print_info, print_error, etc.) currently use raw println\!/eprintln\! which will interleave with active spinners. When spinners are wired into more commands, these need to route through self.mp.println()/self.mp.suspend() to avoid visual corruption. Also remove #[allow(dead_code)] from the mp field and EventProcessor::display() accessor when used.
close_reason: Static output routed through MultiProgress

title: Wire ErrorCollector into event processing
description: Phase 2 of indicatif display layer: use DisplayManager::collect_error() and ErrorDetail to accumulate structured errors during multi-package operations, then print a copy-pasteable error summary at the end via DisplayManager::finish(). Currently ErrorDetail, ErrorCollector, collect_error(), and has_errors() exist but are unused (#[allow(dead_code)]). Remove the annotations when wired up. The EventProcessor already calls display.finish() after processing.
close_reason: JoinError metadata fix and ErrorCollector wiring implemented

title: Wire spinners into install/check/validate commands
description: Phase 2 of indicatif display layer: use DisplayManager::start_operation() and OperationHandle for animated spinners in install, check, and validate commands. Currently these commands use static print_progress() calls. The spinner infrastructure (start_operation, finish_success/failure/warning, OperationHandle) exists but is only used by the list command. Remove #[allow(dead_code)] from start_operation(), OperationHandle struct/impl, and the non-in-place finish methods when wired up.
close_reason: Duplicate of selfie-v5a, resolved in same commit

title: Graceful shutdown with tokio::signal — use existing PackageEvent::Canceled
description:
Implement Ctrl+C (SIGINT) handling using tokio::signal::ctrl_c() (already have tokio as a dependency — no new crate needed).

Current state: No signal handling exists. Ctrl+C during install orphans subprocesses. process::exit() is called in main.rs without cleanup. The PackageEvent::Canceled event type already exists in the event system but is never emitted by service code. The event processor already handles it (sets exit_code=1, prints warning).

Key changes needed:
- main.rs: Wrap dispatch_command in tokio::select! with ctrl_c() signal
- service.rs: Accept a CancellationToken (from tokio_util) or similar mechanism to propagate cancellation to spawned tasks
- shell.rs: On cancellation, kill running subprocess via child.kill().await and emit Canceled event

Note: spawned tasks currently use tokio::spawn() without retaining JoinHandle — this pattern needs adjustment for clean shutdown.

Depends on: Nothing, but this is the largest of the 5 items.
close_reason: Implemented graceful Ctrl+C shutdown with CancellationToken threaded through service and command runner layers

title: Add strum crate — derive Display/FromStr for enums
description:
Replace 10 hand-written impl Display for ... blocks with #[derive(strum::Display)].

Targets:
- event/metadata.rs: OperationType (7 match arms)
- event.rs: StepCount, OperationFailure, CommandFailure, DependencyFailure, OperationSuccess, CheckResult, ValidationStatus
- commands/runner.rs: OutputChunk
- validation.rs: ValidationErrorCategory (6 match arms)

Note: Some Display impls have complex formatting (e.g., CommandFailure includes exit code). strum supports #[strum(to_string = "...")] for simple cases but complex multi-field formatting should stay hand-written. Assess each impl individually.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add semver crate — replace hand-rolled version regex (may drop regex)
description:
Replace regex::Regex::new(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+") in package/validate.rs:164-167 with semver::Version::parse().

Behavior change: Current regex is permissive — 1.2.3xyz passes, pre-release like 1.2.3-beta passes. semver::Version::parse() is stricter (proper semver spec). This is the correct behavior for a version validation warning. Note the validation produces a warning, not an error, so stricter is fine.

Bonus: regex is used nowhere else in the codebase. Adopting semver lets us drop regex entirely (heavy transitive deps: regex-automata, regex-syntax, aho-corasick).

Maintained by dtolnay. Used by Cargo itself.
close_reason: Replaced regex with semver crate for version validation

title: Make selfie crate re-exports consistent
description: Several public types in the selfie crate are not re-exported from their parent modules, forcing consumers to use deep paths like selfie::fs::filesystem::FileSystemError instead of selfie::fs::FileSystemError. Audit all pub mod/pub use in the selfie crate and add re-exports so that commonly-used types are accessible from the module they logically belong to (e.g., fs::FileSystemError, package::event::error::StreamedError). This improves ergonomics for CLI and future consumer crates.
close_reason: Added pub use re-exports in event.rs, config.rs, fs.rs, and package.rs. Updated all CLI imports and doc examples to use shorter paths. Code reviewed and all issues fixed.

title: Fix 3 failing package_list_tests integration tests
description:
Three integration tests in crates/cli/tests/package_list_tests.rs are failing due to assertion mismatches on display formatting:

1. test_package_list_all_flag_not_relevant_status - expects 'No check' but gets 'N/A'
2. test_package_list_default_behavior_filters_by_environment - expects 'No check' but gets 'N/A'
3. test_package_list_environment_mismatch_shows_stats - expects 'No packages found for environment' but output format differs

These are pre-existing failures unrelated to the EventStream unification work.
close_reason: Fixed both bugs: status None vs NoCheckCommand, and environment_stats computed before filtering

title: Dual file-discovery code paths in YamlPackageRepository
description: YamlPackageRepository has two separate code paths for finding .yml/.yaml files: find_package_files (on the trait) uses path_exists twice, while find_package_files_with_context (internal, used by get_package) uses list_directory. The logic for resolving .yml vs .yaml extensions exists twice and should be unified — one should call the other.
close_reason: Unified in commit 1fb4df4: extracted filter_matching_packages as shared pure function, both find_package_files and find_package_files_with_context now use it.

title: Consider 'which' crate for command availability checks
description: ShellCommandRunner::is_command_available spawns a shell process to run 'command -v'. The 'which' crate can do this natively without spawning a process — faster and avoids shell-related edge cases. Would also eliminate the default timeout wait (60s) for simple availability checks.
close_reason: Replaced shell-based is_command_available with which crate for native PATH lookup

title: PackageParseError::FileSystemError erases source error to String
description: PackageParseError::FileSystemError converts the source FileSystemError to a String (source_message: String), losing the error chain. Other error types in the codebase preserve #[source] for proper error chain propagation. This variant should store the original error or at least an Arc<FileSystemError> to maintain the chain.
close_reason: Replaced source_message: String with #[source] source: Arc<FileSystemError> to preserve error chain

title: Package pub(crate) fields accessed inconsistently — direct access vs accessors
description: Package has pub(crate) fields with accessor methods, but internal code inconsistently uses direct field access (e.g., package.name, package.environments) vs the public accessor methods (e.g., package.name(), package.environments()). Should standardize to always use accessors, then tighten field visibility.
close_reason: GetPackage fields are now pub(crate) with consistent accessor methods; CLI uses accessors everywhere

title: Emoji handling inconsistent — install.rs hard-codes emoji outside TerminalProgressReporter
description: Most emoji/styling goes through TerminalProgressReporter, but install.rs hard-codes 📦 and 🔧 directly in InstallationDisplay::add_output_line. All emoji should be handled consistently through TerminalProgressReporter to respect --no-color and terminal capability detection.
close_reason: Routed all emoji in install.rs through TerminalProgressReporter with proper console::Emoji fallbacks and use_colors support

title: Replace unsafe NonZeroU64::new_unchecked with safe const
description: config.rs:50 and config.rs:64 use unsafe { NonZeroU64::new_unchecked(60) } and unsafe { NonZeroUsize::new_unchecked(4) } for compile-time constants. Since Rust 1.83, these can be replaced with safe const blocks: const { NonZeroU64::new(60).unwrap() } which fails at compile time if zero is passed. No reason to use unsafe here.
close_reason: Replaced unsafe NonZero with safe const blocks

title: Fix typos: ApplyToConfg and SUGGESTION_EJOJI
description: Two naming typos in the codebase: (1) ApplyToConfg trait in config/loader.rs is missing an 'i' — should be ApplyToConfig. Used in loader.rs, main.rs, and cli/config.rs. (2) SUGGESTION_EJOJI constant in terminal_progress_reporter.rs should be SUGGESTION_EMOJI.
close_reason: Renamed ApplyToConfg→ApplyToConfig (4 files) and SUGGESTION_EJOJI→SUGGESTION_EMOJI (1 file). All checks pass.

title: Extract handle_missing_environment to steps.rs (DRY)
description: handle_missing_environment is duplicated verbatim in check.rs:123 and install.rs:328. The error construction and event sending are identical; only the return type differs. This should be extracted to steps.rs as a shared function.
close_reason: Extracted handle_missing_environment to steps.rs with generic <T>, removed Box::new+deref anti-pattern in handle_missing_check_command, made function sync instead of needlessly async

title: Address verbose/use_colors in library AppConfig
description: AppConfig contains verbose and use_colors fields which are purely presentation concerns -- the library doesn't use them for any logic. They exist solely so the CLI can read them back out after loading config. Options: (1) split into CoreConfig + UI config, (2) document that these are consumed by UI layers. Either way, clarify the boundary for v1.
close_reason: Split AppConfig into SelfieConfig (library) and CliConfig (CLI). Library no longer contains verbose/use_colors. Config file supports sectioned format with cli: section.

title: Unify PackageService method return types
description: Some service methods return EventStream directly (check, install) while others return Result<EventStream, PackageError> (info, validate, list, create). The Result wrapper on the latter group adds nothing since the inner call never fails -- they all wrap with Ok(self.execute_operation_with_deps(...)). Pick one approach for API consistency before v1.
close_reason: Already implemented — all PackageService methods now uniformly return EventStream directly

title: Investigate TOML as alternative config format
description: TOML is the Rust ecosystem standard (Cargo.toml). Evaluate whether it would be a better fit than YAML for selfie package specs. Consider: first-class Rust serde support, familiarity for Rust users, handling of nested structures (environments with commands/deps), comments support, no type coercion footguns. Main concern: TOML can be verbose for deeply nested structures like per-environment install/check commands with dependencies.

title: Investigate Nickel as alternative config format
description: Nickel (nickel-lang.org) is a configuration language written in Rust with gradual typing and contracts. Evaluate whether it would be a better fit than YAML for selfie package specs. Consider: Rust-native (no external runtime), built-in validation via contracts, human-readability for hand-edited files, learning curve for users, ecosystem maturity, serde integration story. Compare with current YAML + serde-saphyr + garde approach.

title: Use spawn_blocking for git CLI calls in async tasks
description: Copilot review flagged that execute_push and pull call synchronous git CLI commands (stage_files, commit, push, fetch, fast_forward) inside tokio async tasks. This can block worker threads during long network ops. Consider wrapping blocking git calls in tokio::task::spawn_blocking, or making the git provider trait async. Low priority — selfie is a personal CLI tool, so thread starvation is unlikely in practice.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add version field to package specs
description: Add an optional version field to package spec files for tracking which version of a package definition the user has. This is about the spec version, not the installed package version. Found in selfie-v3 old repo.
close_reason: User decided against this — version field was recently removed intentionally

title: Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM during installs
description: Handle SIGINT/SIGTERM signals gracefully during long-running install operations. Should clean up any in-progress state and exit cleanly rather than leaving partial installations. Found as planned (but not implemented) in selfie-v3 old repo.
close_reason: Added SIGTERM handling alongside existing SIGINT, plus user-facing cancellation message

title: Add file logging with rotation support
description: Add optional file logging with configuration for log directory, max files, and max file size. Useful for debugging issues after the fact. The old selfie-v3 repo had --log-enable, --log-directory, --log-max-files, --log-max-size flags. Current repo uses tracing but has no file logging configuration.

title: Move collect_all_packages inside spawned task for immediate stream return
description: collect_all_packages() currently runs before create_event_stream(), which delays the Started event and blocks the caller while parsing YAML files. Moving package collection inside the spawned task would let the stream return immediately. Low priority for typical workloads (~50 YAML files) but would improve responsiveness for large repos. Flagged by Copilot review on PR #33.

title: JoinError emits PackageListItem with empty version and environments
description: In service/list.rs:160, on JoinError the emitted PackageListItem uses an empty version and environments. The CLI list renderer formats 'v{version}', so this displays as just 'v' with no environment context. Since the original package metadata is available from PackageListReady, the error completion item should preserve at least version and environments while setting status = Error(...).
close_reason: JoinError metadata fix and ErrorCollector wiring implemented

title: Route list command summary through DisplayManager
description: P4: The summary at the end of list (list.rs:215-234) uses bare println\! for 'Package directory: ...' and count summaries. Will break when Phase 2 spinners arrive. Also uses no symbols/colors for summary counts, making it visually flat. Route through DisplayManager for consistency.
close_reason: list.rs summary already routed through DisplayManager in 8d1 (PR #23)

title: Deduplicate spinner initialization code
description: P4: start_operation and start_list_spinner (display_manager.rs:365-417) are identical except for max_output_lines: 5 vs 0. Should be a single method with a parameter or a builder pattern.
close_reason: Implemented in commit a8ac5ff on feat/cli-display-consistency branch

title: Add human-panic crate — friendly panic messages (CLI only)
description:
Add human_panic::setup_panic!() as the first line in main() (crates/cli/src/main.rs). Replaces raw stack traces with user-friendly crash report files.

Effort: Minimal — one line + one dep in CLI Cargo.toml.
close_reason: Closed

title: Evaluate 'tabled' crate for derive-macro table formatting
description: tables.rs manually builds tables with comfy-table. The 'tabled' crate offers derive macros for table formatting directly from structs, which could reduce the manual table-building code. Evaluate whether switching or using tabled would simplify output formatting.

title: Consider 'indicatif' crate for progress display
description:
indicatif is by mitsuhiko (same author as console crate already in use), ensuring compatibility. Would only be used in CLI crate (library boundary rule preserved). Current progress is text-only emoji prefixes via TerminalProgressReporter and ProgressTracker; indicatif adds spinners, progress bars, and MultiProgress for future parallel installs.

Evaluate whether indicatif would simplify the current progress code and improve UX for long-running operations like package installation.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete: replaced TerminalProgressReporter with indicatif-powered DisplayManager. PR #16 targets uat branch. Phase 2 (wiring spinners into event handlers) can be a follow-up issue.

title: PackageRepoError boxing requires manual Box::new at every error site
description: PackageRepoError::PackageError(Box<PackageError>) requires callers to write Box::new(PackageError::Foo { .. }).into() at every error site. A From<PackageError> for PackageRepoError impl that auto-boxes would be cleaner and reduce boilerplate.
close_reason: Added From<PackageError> for PackageRepoError impl and simplified all call sites

title: TerminalProgressReporter methods inconsistently take self vs &self
description: TerminalProgressReporter is a Copy struct (contains only a bool), but its methods inconsistently take self (consuming Copy) vs &self (borrowing). While harmless for Copy types, it's visually inconsistent and should be standardized to &self throughout.
close_reason: Closed

title: Clean up dead test helpers in test-common
description: Several fixture functions in test-common/src/fixtures.rs are defined but never imported or used by any test file: create_multi_env_package_file, create_incomplete_package_file, create_custom_package_file, create_failing_package_file, and create_slow_package_file. These should be removed to keep the test infrastructure lean.
close_reason: Removed 5 dead fixture functions from test-common/fixtures.rs (create_multi_env_package_file, create_incomplete_package_file, create_custom_package_file, create_failing_package_file, create_slow_package_file). Committed in 5202d84.

title: Remove async_trait from synchronous FileSystem trait
description: filesystem.rs:22 applies #[async_trait::async_trait] to the FileSystem trait, but all methods are synchronous fn, not async fn. The macro is misleading and unnecessary. It should be removed.
close_reason: Removed #[async_trait::async_trait] from FileSystem trait. All methods were synchronous; the macro was misleading and unnecessary.
